Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Diego CA
1131 AM PST Sat Nov 21 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Dry weather prevails through Sunday morning. A weak weather system 
moves in from the northwest, bringing a chance for light 
precipitation for parts of Southern California by Sunday evening 
into early Monday morning. Cooler and drier weather will continue 
for Tuesday and Wednesday. High pressure will move into the region 
by Thanksgiving Day into later next week, bringing warmer weather.

&&

.DISCUSSION...FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO 
COUNTIES...

Light offshore flow has been observed late this morning, with 
highest gusts across the San Diego County mts with gusts up to 35 
MPH. Winds will be easing into the afternoon as a weak ridge drifts 
over the Desert Southwest. Similar temperatures can be expected into 
Sunday with greater onshore flow. A weak shortwave will cross over 
the region later on Sunday into early Monday bringing the chance for 
light precipitation, first at the coast and then pushing into the 
coastal slopes. Models are in fair agreement about light rain 
starting for areas near the coast sometime around the sunset hour,
a bit later further inland. The forecast remains on track for 
light accumulations overall with one tenth of an inch to no rain 
at all, locally higher in heavier showers. Though snow levels will
be near 5,000 feet, the presence of relatively drier air will 
make it difficult for much accumulation. Most areas above 5,000 
will see a dusting to near one inch for higher mountains. 
Precipitation will end from the north to south on Monday morning 
with more sunshine by the afternoon.

Another weak ridge tries to develop on Tuesday, where cooler 
temperatures remain under mostly sunny skies. At the same time, a 
stronger low pressure system will move into the the Pacific 
Northwest coastline. As it does so, models indicate a shortwave will 
break off from the main flow of the system and drift southward 
across California. Most model consensus shows this system becoming 
weaker, and not making it very far south. This evidence is also 
shown in a drying trend that has been noticed for Wednesday, where 
precipitation chances have become more limited. Confidence is 
increasing on a dry day for many with temperatures a degree or two 
warmer from Tuesday. 

Model consensus on what becomes of the system mentioned above is 
still in somewhat of question. Confidence continues to be high that 
Thanksgiving Day will be dry and calm. Most models bring an 
expanding ridge from the south over the region, keeping the 
Wednesday weather system away from the region by Thanksgiving and 
beyond. If this occurs, relatively quiet weather with somewhat 
warmer weather and weak offshore flow along the coastal slopes. Some 
member of the GFS show a more outlier pattern, with the weather 
system forming into a closed low over Arizona. If this occurs, the 
pressure gradient would tighten, leading to more elevated Santa Ana 
winds into the valleys with even warmer weather. NBM for now shows 
highs mainly in the 70s and lower 80s for the valleys west of the 
mountains. Yet another area of low pressure moves closer to the West 
Coast by next weekend. This will bring a cooling trend, but where 
this system goes and if it will bring any additional precipitation 
to our region is still uncertain.

&&

.AVIATION... 
211800Z...VFR prevails with gradually increasing high clouds 
throughout the day. Lower clouds near 5000ft MSL increase near the 
coasts Sunday afternoon, with VCSH arriving in the vicinity of KSAN 
closer to 00z Monday.

&&

.MARINE...
No marine hazards are expected through Tuesday.

The next storm system and associated swell is forecast to move into 
the region Wednesday afternoon into Thursday, which could increase 
wind and wave heights back to hazardous levels. There remains 
uncertainty in the forecast track/strength of this storm, but at 
this time, winds may gust up to 25 kts with seas of 8-12 feet.

&&

.BEACHES...
Morning high tides will be on the increase next week, exceeding 7 
feet by Sunday. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, with 
the King Tides peaking on Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning 
on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet. Background surf 
on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, 
but an incoming swell Wednesday afternoon into Thursday could bring 
notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. There remains uncertainty 
in the forecast swell Wednesday-Thursday, but surf may reach 6-8 
feet Thursday morning, locally up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

A Coastal Flood Advisory remains in effect for Sunday morning 
through Tuesday morning for the rising high tides, with a Coastal 
Flood Watch in effect for Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon.

NOTE: Forecast tides have been adjusted above baseline astronomical 
predictions accordingly, based on trends in recent observations.

&&

.SKYWARN... 
Skywarn activation is not requested. However weather spotters are
encouraged to report significant weather conditions.
